rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons are an open subset showing locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary appears in both authority files.
Every individual INSPIRE polygon has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
A single registered title number may contain several separate polygons.
The definitive extent of a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons and requires the individual title plan.
A missing INSPIRE ID may indicate unregistered land, leasehold registration or another tenure excluded from the dataset.
OGL reuse requires HM Land Registry Crown copyright and database-rights attribution.
Reusing polygon geometry and X/Y coordinates also requires the stated Ordnance Survey attribution.
Exact current Barnet and Enfield GML hrefs, bytes and hashes remain unavailable because the download view redirects.
Current INSPIRE IDs and native-BNG containment for all three candidates remain unresolved.
Each entity response includes a name field.
Each entity response includes the dataset it belongs to.
Each entity response includes a start-date field.
Entity geometry is returned in Well-Known Text form.
Entity point data is returned in Well-Known Text form.
Listed-building entities include grade without requiring a separate query.
The current guide says all 337 local planning authorities can be fetched with entity IDs in one request.
The geometry_entity parameter filters using another entity's stored geometry instead of pasting a raw polygon.
The planning-application data specification is currently in development and may change.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to that specification.
Exact current title-boundary responses for references 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remain unavailable.
Exact current point-intersection responses for the three candidate coordinates remain unavailable.
Authoritative UPRNs bound to the three candidates remain unavailable.
LiDAR Composite download ZIPs now contain the spatial metadata index in GeoPackage rather than Shapefile format.
The GeoPackage metadata index describes the spatial location of raster elevation data.
The GeoPackage metadata index describes the temporal extent of raster elevation data.
Technical guides for the index format and attribute schema are linked from the relevant metadata record.
The Composite products changed delivery format from ASCII to GeoTIFF.
The official guidance says GeoTIFF volumes are about five times smaller on average.
GeoTIFF delivery enabled image services and WCS services for browser, GIS and geoprocessing use.
The exact DTM 1m WCS coverage identifier remains unavailable because the XML body cannot be parsed by the current transport.
Exact TQ2892 pixels and their source-survey lineage remain unavailable.
The grid-supply GML carries location metadata needed to interpret the accompanying ASCII grid.
The grid-supply GML carries grid-spacing metadata.
The grid-supply GML carries the vertical reference system in software-independent form.
The tile-name .asc file contains Esri ASCII grid data.
The tile-name .prj file contains the spatial reference system in Esri format.
The .asc.aux.xml file supplies parameters for consistent default styling in Esri applications.
The per-tile Metadata XML provides details such as flying date.
Mean high and low water breaklines use constant heights based on a local tide-table average for each tile.
The GML model uses mean high/low water springs categories for Scotland, distinct from England and Wales.
The exact current Terrain50 area=TQ download response remains unavailable.
Current TQ29 archive bytes, nested file inventory and cryptographic hashes remain unavailable.
The actual Terrain 50 target cells for the three candidate locations remain unavailable.
